Delhi Police Special Cell Investigates Controversial Anti-Government Posters Found on Airport Express Metro Line

Incident Details on the Airport Express Line

Delhi Police have launched an official investigation after controversial posters questioning government policies were discovered inside a train on the Delhi Metro Airport Express Line. The discovery prompted immediate action by metro operations staff and law enforcement agencies, with the Delhi Police Special Cell joining the inquiry alongside local station police.

According to official police complaints, the incident occurred on October 20. Tarun Chaudhary, a train operator on duty along the Airport Express Line, arrived at the Yashobhoomi metro station at approximately 7:15 PM. During a routine internal inspection of the train cabin, Chaudhary noticed two posters affixed to a passenger seat.

Content of the Discovered Posters

Upon finding the material, the train operator immediately alerted transit authorities and the Operation Control Center. The posters were subsequently handed over to the station controller at Dwarka Sector-21, who reported the matter to law enforcement.

Police sources revealed specific details regarding the text printed on the retrieved materials:

  • First Poster: Contained phrases such as "You can change your own life," "Voting protest," "Spectrum of engagement," and "Community building reform." It also featured a call to action inviting individuals to join a WhatsApp group via an integrated QR code.
  • Second Poster: Bore the heading "Dissatisfied? You are not alone" and featured direct questions regarding government initiatives and public campaigns.

Official Response and Investigation

The IGI Airport metro police station has seized both posters and registered a formal case against unknown individuals. Alongside local police efforts, the Delhi Police Special Cell is actively probing the matter to determine the origin of the posters and identify those responsible for placing them inside the secure metro area.

Practical Implications and Verification

For daily commuters and the general public, this incident highlights ongoing security protocols across transit networks. While metro operations continue as scheduled, authorities are reviewing security measures to prevent unauthorized materials inside coaches.

What is Confirmed vs. Unknown

  • Confirmed: Two posters questioning government policies and featuring a QR code were found on an Airport Express Line train on October 20 by an operator. A police case has been registered by the IGI Airport metro police, and the Special Cell is investigating.
  • Unknown: The identity of the individuals who placed the posters, the exact purpose behind the WhatsApp group linked via the QR code, and whether similar materials were placed elsewhere remain under investigation.

How to Verify

Readers can monitor official updates and verified reports regarding this ongoing police investigation through major news outlets and official statements released by Delhi Police.
